title: Refinement square for compatible semilinear compact-support compositors
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes below are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. On a small representative of $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ put $B_{n,W}=(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathscr S_W$ consist of $B_{n,W}$-module sheaves with semilinear quotient transitions and compatible componentwise morphisms. Use $D(\mathscr S_W)$ and the simultaneous geometric section models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Write $P_u=u^*$, $R_u=Ru_*$, with unit $\eta_u$ and counit $\varepsilon_u$ of $P_u\dashv R_u$, and $J_j=j_!$ for exact open extension. All maps below are actual derived-system maps with their quotient transitions.

Let $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$ be separated finite type. For $a=1,2$ choose compatible triangles $j_a:X\hookrightarrow V_a$, $b_a:V_a\hookrightarrow\overline X_a$, $i_a:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y_a$, with $q_a:V_a\to Y$, $p_a:\overline X_a\to\overline Y_a$, $s_a:\overline Y_a\to Z$ proper, $q_aj_a=f$, $s_ai_a=g$, and $p_ab_a=i_aq_a$ Cartesian, i.e. $V_a\cong\overline X_a\times_{\overline Y_a}Y$ via $(b_a,q_a)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements, def-pc-fibre-product]. Put $F_a=R_{q_a}J_{j_a}$, $G_a=R_{s_a}J_{i_a}$, $H_a=R_{s_ap_a}J_{b_aj_a}$. Let $\beta_a:G_aF_a\to H_a$ be the proper/open-compositor word of [lem-pur-system-compatible-compositor-normalization].
Suppose proper maps $u:\overline Y_1\to\overline Y_2$, $v:\overline X_1\to\overline X_2$, $w:V_1\to V_2$ satisfy $ui_1=i_2$, $s_2u=s_1$, $vb_1=b_2w$, $wj_1=j_2$, $q_2w=q_1$, and $p_2v=up_1$. For each induced refinement $t:c_1\to c_2$ with proper factors $r_1=r_2t$, define
$$\theta_t=R_{r_2}(\gamma_t^{-1})c_{r_2,t},$$
where $\gamma_t:J_{j_2}\to R_tJ_{j_1}$ is the intrinsic proper/open mate and $c_{r_2,t}:R_{r_1}\cong R_{r_2}R_t$ is the canonical compositor [lem-pur-system-compactification-pf-substitution, def-sf-refinement-comparison-isomorphism]. Write $\theta_f:F_1\to F_2$, $\theta_g:G_1\to G_2$, $\theta_h:H_1\to H_2$ for the three comparisons. On systems $M$ with bounded constructible levels [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] one has
$$\theta_{h,M}\beta_{1,M}=\beta_{2,M}\,G_2(\theta_{f,M})\,\theta_{g,F_1M}.$$
Every finite collection of compatible triangles admits a common dominating compatible triangle; comparison through it is independent of the common refinement and is transitive. Consequently these words identify with the geometric compact-support compositor for any specified compactification choices, by these exact refinement maps. The assertions hold before evaluation, without uniform bounds in $n$. Evaluation carries these comparisons and this equation to the specified finite refinements and composition comparison of [thm-sf-comp-composition].

proof.text: Work in the actual derived categories of semilinear systems, using [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Evaluation identifies $F_aM$ with the finite compactification candidate $Rq_{a*}j_{a!}M_n$. Each $M_n$ has a bounded etale-origin witness by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]; [prop-finite-compact-support-constructibility] therefore makes each $(F_aM)_n$ bounded constructible as well. Consequently [lem-pur-system-compactification-pf-substitution] supplies the invertible comparisons for $f,h$ on $M$ and for $g$ on both $F_aM$. Put $\rho_f=\theta_f^{-1}$, $\rho_g=\theta_g^{-1}$ and $\rho_h=\theta_h^{-1}$. By their specified definitions these are the forward proper/open mates followed by proper composition. The two $\beta_a$ are the system maps and isomorphisms of [lem-pur-system-compatible-compositor-normalization]. These applications impose separate bounds at each $n$, not a bound on the whole system.

proof.text:
Name the proper/open squares $A=(j_1,j_2,1_X,w)$, $D=(i_1,i_2,1_Y,u)$, $E=(b_1j_1,b_2j_2,1_X,v)$, $F=(b_1,b_2,w,v)$, and $Q_a=(b_a,i_a,q_a,p_a)$; a tuple lists top open, bottom open, left proper, right proper. Set $a=\Gamma_A$, $d=\Gamma_D$, $e=\Gamma_E$, $z=\Gamma_F$, and $t_a=\Gamma_{Q_a}$. All the required properness and commutation equations are hypotheses; in particular $F$ need not be Cartesian. Horizontal pasting in [lem-sf-semilinear-proper-open-mate-pasting] gives
$$e=(zJ_{j_1})\circ(J_{b_2}a).$$
Its vertical pasting, applied to the two decompositions of the rectangle $(b_1,i_2,q_1,up_1=p_2v)$, gives
$$(R_ut_1)\circ(dR_{q_1})=(R_{p_2}z)\circ(t_2R_w).$$
Here and below insert the canonical proper and open compositors; [lem-sf-semilinear-compositor-coherence] makes these identifications associative, natural and unital. The mates are the intrinsic ones used in the displayed definitions of the refinement and triangle comparisons, including for the non-Cartesian refinement squares.

proof.text:
Under those compositors the defining words are $\beta_a=R_{s_a}t_aJ_{j_a}$, $\rho_f=R_{q_2}a$, $\rho_g=R_{s_2}d$, and $\rho_h=R_{s_2}R_{p_2}e$. Using the two pasting equations of [lem-sf-semilinear-proper-open-mate-pasting], compute
$$\begin{aligned}
\rho_h\beta_2
&=R_{s_2}R_{p_2}(zJ_{j_1})\,R_{s_2}R_{p_2}(J_{b_2}a)\,R_{s_2}(t_2J_{j_2})\\
&=R_{s_2}\big((R_{p_2}z)(t_2R_w)J_{j_1}\big)\,R_{s_2}(J_{i_2}R_{q_2}a)\\
&=R_{s_2}(R_ut_1J_{j_1})\,R_{s_2}(dR_{q_1}J_{j_1})\,R_{s_2}(J_{i_2}R_{q_2}a)\\
&=\beta_1\,\rho_{g,F_1}\,G_2(\rho_f).
\end{aligned}$$
The second equality is precisely naturality of $t_2$ at $a:J_{j_2}\to R_wJ_{j_1}$; its source and target are obtained using $q_2w=q_1$. The third is the vertical equation of Step 2. The first uses the horizontal equation for $e$. The final equality uses $s_2u=s_1$ and the named words, with [lem-sf-semilinear-compositor-coherence]. Thus no equality of system maps has been inferred from evaluation.

proof.text:
Evaluate the preceding identity on $M$, postcompose with $\theta_{h,M}$, and precompose with $G_2(\theta_{f,M})\theta_{g,F_1M}$. Functoriality gives $G_2(\rho_{f,M})G_2(\theta_{f,M})=1$, while $\rho_{g,F_1M}\theta_{g,F_1M}=1$ and $\theta_{h,M}\rho_{h,M}=1$. The result is exactly
$$\theta_{h,M}\beta_{1,M}=\beta_{2,M}G_2(\theta_{f,M})\theta_{g,F_1M}.$$
All cancelled inverses exist by Step 1.

proof.text: For the finite common-domination clause, use the already proved Compactification.Triangle.inf, infFst and infSnd from WeilConjectures.Compactification.Triangle directly. A Triangle.Hom forgets to SystemTriangleRefinement by reversing q_comm and p_comm. Compose SystemTriangleRefinement records componentwise; associativity and the two cross equations prove the cross equations of the composite. Induct on a finite set of triangles: for an insertion take the binary inf of the previous common triangle with the inserted triangle, and compose the first projection with the old legs. For the empty set use Triangle.ofHasCompactification f g; Nagata supplies its compactifications since Z is qcqs, as follows from its finite-type field structure. Apply this construction to the finite image of the given family; it includes empty and repeated families. For systemCompositorInChoices_exists, densely compactify c.g followed by d.i. The proved proper/open dense-compactification Cartesian lemma in Compactification.OverRefinement gives a triangle S with cf=c and cg=d. Separately form the source Triangle.ofRestrict d (e.ofComp d); its total compactification refines e by the image inclusion followed by the first pullback projection. Take the binary common triangle of S and this latter triangle. Its first projection supplies the required f and g refinements, and its second total projection composed with the displayed refinement supplies the required gf leg. Every chosen existential witness is used only to prove an existential theorem; no data definition is introduced.

proof.text: For a common triangle $T$ mapping to triangles $a,b$, compare each of the three compact-support functors by $C_x(a,b)=\theta_{x,T\to b}\theta_{x,T\to a}^{-1}$, for $x=f,g,h$. The common-refinement independence and cocycle clause of [lem-pur-system-compactification-pf-substitution] says that each $C_x$ is independent of the common compactification and that $C_x(b,c)C_x(a,b)=C_x(a,c)$. Apply Step 4 to $T\to a$ and $T\to b$ and cancel the three invertible comparisons. This identifies $\beta_a$ and $\beta_b$ by precisely $C_f,C_g,C_h$. Comparing any two common triangles using Step 5 gives the same result; transitivity follows from the displayed cocycle. For arbitrary specified choices of the compactifications of $f,g,gf$, conjugate $\beta_T$ by these three comparisons. This is independent of $T$ and uses exactly the stated refinement maps. By [lem-pur-system-compatible-compositor-normalization], $\beta_T$ itself is the geometric composition word, so the conjugate is its expression in the specified choices. The Lean proof of systemSpanComparison_trans uses independence three times to replace the three supplied spans by spans on inf c₁₂ c₂₃, with the same middle leg u.comp b₁₂. Expanding systemSpanComparison then cancels the adjacent theta-middle and its inverse using the standard Iso associativity and cancellation lemmas. It requires no separate composition-law proof for theta.

proof.text: Finally evaluate the constructed maps at $n$. By [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], evaluation preserves the specified adjunction words, their compositions and proper/open exchanges; being a functor it also preserves each inverse used here. The finite-normalization clause of [lem-sf-semilinear-proper-open-mate-pasting] therefore sends $\gamma_t$ to the specified finite proper/open refinement mate. The etale-origin hypotheses it requires hold by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] and Step 1. The evaluation clause of [lem-pur-system-compatible-compositor-normalization] sends $\beta_T$ to the specified $\alpha_{g,f}$ of [thm-sf-comp-composition]. Hence evaluation of Step 4 and of the conjugations of Step 6 is exactly the finite refinement/composition equation. All equalities were already proved before evaluation, and no uniform cohomological interval or faithfulness on morphisms has been used.
